prior_decision.quote: Thus, the replication of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria. Mean response latencies by target age and target race for all six emotional transitions are displayed in Figure 1. For the happy-to-angry transition, analysis revealed a significant two-way interaction between target age and target race, F(1, 54) = 4.07, p = .049, η²p = 0.07. When observing Black targets, participants saw anger appear sooner on a young (M = 11.14 s, SD = 3.84 s) as compared to an old face (M = 12.17, SD = 3.92 s), t(54) = -2.61, p = .012, d = -0.35. The opposite, however not significant pattern was found for White targets, such that participants judged anger as appearing sooner on an old (M = 10.68 s, SD = 3.38) as compared to a young face (M = 13.34 s, SD = 12.70 s), t(54) = 1.47, p = .15. These results are not in line with the original study and our stated hypotheses, which predicted that for White targets, participants would judge anger as appearing significantly sooner on an old than on a young face.
